question.text: At the quarterly investment committee meeting of Tejas Growth Equity Fund, partner Mr. Vikram Rao is reviewing the deal funnel. 'Deal sourcing' as a key role of the AIF Investment Manager MOST accurately refers to:

answer.text: Identifying favourable investment opportunities, networking with investment bankers, CAs, corporate advisers and policy makers to generate and close deals that support future fundraises.
The RTA generating a monthly subscription report.
The custodian settling purchase trades within T+1.
The merchant banker filing the PPM with SEBI.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7, deal sourcing is a core manager role: 'An AIF manager must identify favourable opportunities, source and complete successful transactions... A significant amount of effort is invested in prospecting for transactions and relationship management with investment bankers, chartered accountants, corporate advisers, consulting firms, senior corporate heads.' Networking builds the pipeline that supports follow-on fund raises. The Trap: Option B is an RTA operational function. Option C is custodian settlement. Option D is the merchant banker's scheme-launch filing role — all adjacent but distinct from manager deal-sourcing. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM) covers security selection, not private-market deal sourcing. XV (Research Analyst) covers the research angle of picking listed securities. XIX-C uniquely covers private-deal origination. Manager's Pro-Tip: Track your deal-funnel conversion ratio (sourced -> screened -> term-sheet -> closed) and present it at every LPAC. A ratio of 100:20:5:1 is healthy; LPs worry if you are closing more than 25% of screened deals (suggests weak filtering).
